legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

variants.title: Buried Control: CHE Program/Source FN Erase
variants.summary: Two sections from Figures 4 and 5 share one FG conductor; control is buried in silicon. Erase coupling remains symbolic; inconsistent read entries in Table 2 are not reproduced.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Cypress Semiconductor: Buried-Control-Gate Single-Poly EEPROM Patent US5844271A
sources.locator: Figures 3–6; buried control electrode, thick/thin oxide regions, and operating descriptions; claim 1
sources.limit: Demonstrates one single-poly EEPROM implementation. It does not establish that current Synopsys MTP uses this structure or the same hot-electron injection and tunneling paths.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Program: Compare Channel Hot-Electron and Source-Side Injection
operations.summary: Source-side injection uses the potential drop at the boundary between the selection and storage regions to energize channel electrons, which are collected by the field toward the floating gate. Source/drain labels and biases must follow the original drawing; injection locations in different structures cannot be interchanged arbitrarily. Higher injection efficiency also does not eliminate the macro's need for voltage boosting, current limiting, or verification.

sources.label: Worldwide Semiconductor Manufacturing / TSMC: Split-Gate Flash Patent US6232180B1
sources.locator: Assignment records from 1999 and 2000; Figure 6 and its operating table; claims 4 and 6
sources.limit: This embodiment uses source-side injection and channel erase. Its operating table must not be combined with SuperFlash inter-gate FN erase in the same cross-section. Aggregated assignee metadata must be checked against the assignment timeline.

sources.label: SST / Microchip: SuperFlash Technology Brochure DS00001425F
sources.locator: Pages 2–3; stacked-gate/split-gate comparison; source-side injection, inter-gate FN erase, and three structural generations
sources.limit: Structures and mechanisms are read in the context of the identified SuperFlash generation. The 2018 shipment figures, node table, and typical reliability data are not guarantees for every product in 2026.

sources.label: Microchip: SST39SF020A Parallel Flash Product Page
sources.kind: Manufacturer Status for an Identified Product
sources.locator: Model, product status, and 2 Mb / 4.5–5.5 V parallel flash summary
sources.limit: Listed as in production when reviewed. The 4.5–5.5 V range is this product's supply range, not an interface voltage for all NOR and certainly not the cell's tunneling bias.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Flash Memory Fundamentals
sources.locator: Figures 2–5; floating-gate and charge-trap storage; threshold voltage and series-string reading
sources.limit: An introductory teaching source, not a complete operating specification for a particular chip. Generic illustrations do not establish the materials and biases of all planar or 3D NAND.

variants.title: Stacked Gate: Drain CHE/Source FN
variants.summary: Corresponds to conventional stacked-gate mechanisms in the background of US6232180B1, not to its proposed split-gate invention.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.limit: This embodiment uses source-side injection and channel erase. Its operating table must not be combined with SuperFlash inter-gate FN erase in the same cross-section. Aggregated assignee metadata must be checked against the assignment timeline.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Erase: Follow the Structure's Electron Exit Path
operations.summary: Two split-gate implementations may have different erase barriers and charge exits, so their terminal voltages cannot be combined into one bias set. Erase scope depends on shared gates, wells, and array control. Updating a byte still requires the product's block-erase and data-preservation flow; fine-grained reading is not equivalent to fine-grained erase.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.limit: This embodiment uses source-side injection and channel erase. Its operating table must not be combined with SuperFlash inter-gate FN erase in the same cross-section. Aggregated assignee metadata must be checked against the assignment timeline.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: SST / Microchip: SuperFlash Technology Brochure DS00001425F
sources.locator: Pages 2–3; stacked-gate/split-gate comparison; source-side injection, inter-gate FN erase, and three structural generations
sources.limit: Structures and mechanisms are read in the context of the identified SuperFlash generation. The 2018 shipment figures, node table, and typical reliability data are not guarantees for every product in 2026.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

variants.title: US6232180B1: SSI/Well-Channel FN
variants.summary: SG is below an overlapping FG; source is raised for program, while SG/S/D float and the well is raised for erase.

operations.title: Read: Sense the Selected Cell's Channel Directly
operations.summary: NOR does not require an entire string of storage cells to conduct before one cell can be read, which favors random access. An overerased stacked-gate cell that conducts while unselected can corrupt the shared bitline; a separate selection function helps shut off that path. Actual latency still includes wordlines, bitlines, sensing, and the external interface, not only individual-cell speed.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: SST / Microchip: SuperFlash Technology Brochure DS00001425F
sources.locator: Pages 2–3; stacked-gate/split-gate comparison; source-side injection, inter-gate FN erase, and three structural generations
sources.limit: Structures and mechanisms are read in the context of the identified SuperFlash generation. The 2018 shipment figures, node table, and typical reliability data are not guarantees for every product in 2026.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

variants.title: US6232180B1: SSI/Well-Channel FN
variants.summary: SG is below an overlapping FG; source is raised for program, while SG/S/D float and the well is raised for erase.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
FG is a floating gate without a DC terminal; Vₜ is threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Worldwide Semiconductor Manufacturing / TSMC: Split-Gate Flash Patent US6232180B1
sources.locator: Assignment records from 1999 and 2000; Figure 6 and its operating table; claims 4 and 6
sources.limit: This embodiment uses source-side injection and channel erase. Its operating table must not be combined with SuperFlash inter-gate FN erase in the same cross-section. Aggregated assignee metadata must be checked against the assignment timeline.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Program: Distinguish Tunneling Capture from Local Hot-Electron Injection
operations.summary: In a tunneling example, charge crosses the thin dielectric from the channel side and is then trapped. In a hot-electron example, carriers first gain energy near the drain, producing localized stored charge. An insulating trapping layer does not automatically equalize potentials and charge distributions as a conductor does. The product page does not disclose the complete film thicknesses and terminal biases, so this explanation remains at the verified mechanism level.

sources.label: NCR: SONOS Blocking-Oxide Patent WO1981000790A1
sources.locator: Figure 1; descriptions of silicon nitride and the upper/lower oxides; claim 1; PCT priority information
sources.limit: Provides an early SONOS stack and retention/program-erase tradeoffs. Its film thicknesses, biases, and cycling results must not be extrapolated to modern SONOS, MONOS, or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Saifun: Asymmetric Charge-Trapping Patent US5768192A
sources.locator: Front page of the original publication; localized hot-electron programming and reverse-read sections; claims 1 and 23
sources.limit: The original publication names Saifun; Spansion Israel in aggregated metadata reflects later corporate history. This patent alone does not establish the erase mechanisms or commercial specifications of every two-bit NROM implementation.

sources.label: Infineon: SONOS Embedded Flash IP Solutions
sources.locator: SONOS technology section; production nodes; 2T cell and FN program/erase; macro-family specification list
sources.limit: The 25 ns, 100,000-cycle, and ten-year retention figures are listed at family level without fully pairing each node, capacity, temperature, and post-cycling retention condition. They are not combined into one guaranteed specification. This evidence does not cover all NROM or 3D NAND implementations.

sources.label: Cypress: SONOS ONO Stack Scaling
sources.locator: Figures 1–3; uniform channel tunneling, electron programming, and hole erase
sources.limit: A named SONOS tunneling example; no equivalence to the stack or biases of a current Infineon macro is asserted.

variants.title: Uniform SONOS: Electron/Hole Tunneling
variants.summary: Storage-transistor detail; Infineon’s 2T cell also has a series selector. Carrier paths follow the public Cypress patent without asserting a current macro’s complete stack.

operations.title: Erase: Follow the Trap Stack and Identified Mechanism
operations.summary: Removal or neutralization of trapped charge depends on barriers, trap depth, and terminal biases. The upper blocking layer suppresses unwanted exchange on the gate side. Knowing only that silicon nitride is used does not identify the terminal through which electrons or holes enter or leave. The Saifun seed reviewed here primarily supports localized programming and reverse reading; it is not used to invent an erase animation for every NROM implementation.

sources.limit: Provides an early SONOS stack and retention/program-erase tradeoffs. Its film thicknesses, biases, and cycling results must not be extrapolated to modern SONOS, MONOS, or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Saifun: Asymmetric Charge-Trapping Patent US5768192A
sources.locator: Front page of the original publication; localized hot-electron programming and reverse-read sections; claims 1 and 23
sources.limit: The original publication names Saifun; Spansion Israel in aggregated metadata reflects later corporate history. This patent alone does not establish the erase mechanisms or commercial specifications of every two-bit NROM implementation.

sources.label: Infineon: SONOS Embedded Flash IP Solutions
sources.locator: SONOS technology section; production nodes; 2T cell and FN program/erase; macro-family specification list
sources.limit: The 25 ns, 100,000-cycle, and ten-year retention figures are listed at family level without fully pairing each node, capacity, temperature, and post-cycling retention condition. They are not combined into one guaranteed specification. This evidence does not cover all NROM or 3D NAND implementations.

sources.label: Cypress: SONOS ONO Stack Scaling
sources.locator: Figures 1–3; uniform channel tunneling, electron programming, and hole erase
sources.limit: A named SONOS tunneling example; no equivalence to the stack or biases of a current Infineon macro is asserted.

sources.label: Saifun: Self-Aligned NROM Programming and Erasure Areas
sources.locator: Figures 4, 8A, 9, and 10–11; band-to-band hole generation and localized hot-hole injection
sources.limit: The pocket implant and local hole path belong to this example; US5768192A is not used as evidence for this erase path.

variants.title: Uniform SONOS: Electron/Hole Tunneling

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Red plus signs are holes; red arrows show hole motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Red plus signs are holes; red arrows show hole motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Saifun: Self-Aligned NROM Programming and Erasure Areas
sources.locator: Figures 4, 8A, 9, and 10–11; band-to-band hole generation and localized hot-hole injection
sources.limit: The pocket implant and local hole path belong to this example; US5768192A is not used as evidence for this erase path.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Read: Sense the SONOS Window and the NROM Direction
operations.summary: Read current travels through the channel; it does not empty all electrons from the nitride. A channel-wide threshold model explains many SONOS operations, but ignoring charge position in a localized cell can obscure why reverse reading works. Read direction must be labeled against the original programming terminals, rather than silently exchanging source and drain names in a drawing.

sources.label: NCR: SONOS Blocking-Oxide Patent WO1981000790A1
sources.locator: Figure 1; descriptions of silicon nitride and the upper/lower oxides; claim 1; PCT priority information
sources.limit: Provides an early SONOS stack and retention/program-erase tradeoffs. Its film thicknesses, biases, and cycling results must not be extrapolated to modern SONOS, MONOS, or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Saifun: Asymmetric Charge-Trapping Patent US5768192A
sources.locator: Front page of the original publication; localized hot-electron programming and reverse-read sections; claims 1 and 23
sources.limit: The original publication names Saifun; Spansion Israel in aggregated metadata reflects later corporate history. This patent alone does not establish the erase mechanisms or commercial specifications of every two-bit NROM implementation.

sources.label: Infineon: SONOS Embedded Flash IP Solutions
sources.locator: SONOS technology section; production nodes; 2T cell and FN program/erase; macro-family specification list
sources.limit: The 25 ns, 100,000-cycle, and ten-year retention figures are listed at family level without fully pairing each node, capacity, temperature, and post-cycling retention condition. They are not combined into one guaranteed specification. This evidence does not cover all NROM or 3D NAND implementations.

sources.label: Cypress: SONOS ONO Stack Scaling
sources.locator: Figures 1–3; uniform channel tunneling, electron programming, and hole erase
sources.limit: A named SONOS tunneling example; no equivalence to the stack or biases of a current Infineon macro is asserted.

variants.title: Uniform SONOS: Electron/Hole Tunneling
variants.summary: Storage-transistor detail; Infineon’s 2T cell also has a series selector. Carrier paths follow the public Cypress patent without asserting a current macro’s complete stack.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Red plus signs are holes; red arrows show hole motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Infineon: SONOS Embedded Flash IP Solutions
sources.locator: SONOS technology section; production nodes; 2T cell and FN program/erase; macro-family specification list
sources.limit: The 25 ns, 100,000-cycle, and ten-year retention figures are listed at family level without fully pairing each node, capacity, temperature, and post-cycling retention condition. They are not combined into one guaranteed specification. This evidence does not cover all NROM or 3D NAND implementations.

sources.label: NCR: SONOS Blocking-Oxide Patent WO1981000790A1
sources.locator: Figure 1; descriptions of silicon nitride and the upper/lower oxides; claim 1; PCT priority information
sources.limit: Provides an early SONOS stack and retention/program-erase tradeoffs. Its film thicknesses, biases, and cycling results must not be extrapolated to modern SONOS, MONOS, or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Cypress: SONOS ONO Stack Scaling
sources.locator: Figures 1–3; uniform channel tunneling, electron programming, and hole erase
sources.limit: A named SONOS tunneling example; no equivalence to the stack or biases of a current Infineon macro is asserted.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

variants.title: Localized NROM: CHE/Reverse Read
variants.summary: S/D keep their programming-time names; reverse read changes bias and current direction without silently renaming terminals.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Saifun: Asymmetric Charge-Trapping Patent US5768192A
sources.locator: Front page of the original publication; localized hot-electron programming and reverse-read sections; claims 1 and 23
sources.limit: The original publication names Saifun; Spansion Israel in aggregated metadata reflects later corporate history. This patent alone does not establish the erase mechanisms or commercial specifications of every two-bit NROM implementation.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Program: Raise the Selected Wordline and Inhibit Other Channels
operations.summary: The early US7696559B2 example uses Vpgm on the selected wordline and lower pass potentials on the others, with channel conditions inhibiting unwanted programming. Both planar and 3D implementations depend on the effective field across the storage layer, not merely the wordline-to-ground voltage. Specific channel boosting, pulse stepping, and selector timing require verification for each implementation.

sources.label: Toshiba: Columnar-Semiconductor Vertical NAND Patent US7696559B2
sources.locator: Figures 2 and 5–9; programming, erase, and bitline-discharge descriptions; claim 1
sources.limit: A specific early columnar-sidewall embodiment. It is not a substitute for every modern gate-all-around cross-section and is not a complete patent history of planar NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Flash Memory Fundamentals
sources.locator: Figures 2–5; floating-gate and charge-trap storage; threshold voltage and series-string reading
sources.limit: An introductory teaching source, not a complete operating specification for a particular chip. Generic illustrations do not establish the materials and biases of all planar or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: Increasing Flash Capacity with Multilevel Cells
sources.locator: Figure 5 and adjacent text; bits per cell, threshold-voltage states, and speed/lifetime tradeoffs
sources.limit: Supports the requirement for 2 to the Nth power distinguishable states to store N bits and the qualitative tradeoffs. It does not provide universal endurance or speed ratios between TLC/QLC generations.

sources.label: Kioxia: Data Retention in the Managed Flash Endurance and Reliability Series
sources.locator: Pages 1–2; P/E cycling, temperature, and data retention
sources.limit: Supports evaluating NAND reliability under combined conditions. NAND values must not be transferred directly to EEPROM, SONOS, or OTP specifications.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Error-Correction Code Technical Brief
sources.locator: Page 1; raw NAND, managed NAND, and the role of ECC
sources.limit: Supports including error management in system comparisons. It does not supply a universal ECC strength, decoding latency, or spare-capacity ratio that can be applied directly throughout this material.

sources.label: Kioxia: Improving Memory-Hole Process Productivity with a New Etch Gas
sources.locator: Sections on memory-hole profile, etch rate, and high-aspect-ratio processing
sources.limit: Describes a specific deep-hole etching study and process bottlenecks. Its improvement figures are not extrapolated to all equipment, stack heights, or production costs.

sources.label: Y. Luo et al.: Early Retention Loss and Process Variation in 3D NAND
sources.locator: Abstract: layer-to-layer process variation, early retention loss, and retention interference
sources.limit: Only the abstract was reviewed to identify research questions. Unreviewed methods, sample counts, and quantitative improvements are not reused, and the distributions are not assumed to apply to all modern 3D NAND.

sources.label: Y. Cai et al.: Read-Disturb Errors in MLC NAND Flash
sources.date: Research account published 2018-05-08; corresponding DSN 2015 work; reviewed 2026-09-10
sources.locator: Abstract: relationships among pass bias, accumulated cycling, and read disturb
sources.limit: Only qualitative relationships are supported by the reviewed abstract. Unreviewed quantitative results are not reused, and 2Y nm MLC samples are not treated as equivalent to modern 3D QLC.

sources.label: Kioxia: BiCS FLASH Principles and Commercial Generations
sources.date: Page includes technical descriptions through 2023; reviewed 2026-09-10
sources.locator: Commercial-generation section; stacked electrodes, memory holes, and charge-storage film in Figures 4–5
sources.limit: 48 layers / 2015, 96 layers / 2018, 112 layers / 2020, and 162 layers / 2022 are the manufacturer's listed commercial history. This page is not treated as the latest 2026 layer-count ranking or a complete specification for each generation.

variants.title: US7696559B2: Vertical String/Electron Tunneling
variants.summary: A string topology with an unfolded local film section. Erase follows source-line raising and electron release, not an asserted GIDL hole mechanism.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Toshiba: Columnar-Semiconductor Vertical NAND Patent US7696559B2
sources.locator: Figures 2 and 5–9; programming, erase, and bitline-discharge descriptions; claim 1
sources.limit: A specific early columnar-sidewall embodiment. It is not a substitute for every modern gate-all-around cross-section and is not a complete patent history of planar NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Flash Memory Fundamentals
sources.locator: Figures 2–5; floating-gate and charge-trap storage; threshold voltage and series-string reading
sources.limit: An introductory teaching source, not a complete operating specification for a particular chip. Generic illustrations do not establish the materials and biases of all planar or 3D NAND.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Erase: Reset the Charge Window of a Shared Block
operations.summary: Erase granularity follows shared wells, channels, and wordline-bias control, and differs from a read page or a host address. Planar floating-gate cells and modern 3D stacks may use different charge-removal or neutralization paths. This material preserves the boundary of the early embodiment and does not present one common-source bias as the erase specification of all NAND.

sources.label: Toshiba: Columnar-Semiconductor Vertical NAND Patent US7696559B2
sources.locator: Figures 2 and 5–9; programming, erase, and bitline-discharge descriptions; claim 1
sources.limit: A specific early columnar-sidewall embodiment. It is not a substitute for every modern gate-all-around cross-section and is not a complete patent history of planar NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Flash Memory Fundamentals
sources.locator: Figures 2–5; floating-gate and charge-trap storage; threshold voltage and series-string reading
sources.limit: An introductory teaching source, not a complete operating specification for a particular chip. Generic illustrations do not establish the materials and biases of all planar or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: Increasing Flash Capacity with Multilevel Cells
sources.locator: Figure 5 and adjacent text; bits per cell, threshold-voltage states, and speed/lifetime tradeoffs
sources.limit: Supports the requirement for 2 to the Nth power distinguishable states to store N bits and the qualitative tradeoffs. It does not provide universal endurance or speed ratios between TLC/QLC generations.

sources.label: Kioxia: Data Retention in the Managed Flash Endurance and Reliability Series
sources.locator: Pages 1–2; P/E cycling, temperature, and data retention
sources.limit: Supports evaluating NAND reliability under combined conditions. NAND values must not be transferred directly to EEPROM, SONOS, or OTP specifications.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Error-Correction Code Technical Brief
sources.locator: Page 1; raw NAND, managed NAND, and the role of ECC
sources.limit: Supports including error management in system comparisons. It does not supply a universal ECC strength, decoding latency, or spare-capacity ratio that can be applied directly throughout this material.

sources.label: Kioxia: Improving Memory-Hole Process Productivity with a New Etch Gas
sources.locator: Sections on memory-hole profile, etch rate, and high-aspect-ratio processing
sources.limit: Describes a specific deep-hole etching study and process bottlenecks. Its improvement figures are not extrapolated to all equipment, stack heights, or production costs.

sources.label: Y. Luo et al.: Early Retention Loss and Process Variation in 3D NAND
sources.locator: Abstract: layer-to-layer process variation, early retention loss, and retention interference
sources.limit: Only the abstract was reviewed to identify research questions. Unreviewed methods, sample counts, and quantitative improvements are not reused, and the distributions are not assumed to apply to all modern 3D NAND.

sources.label: Y. Cai et al.: Read-Disturb Errors in MLC NAND Flash
sources.date: Research account published 2018-05-08; corresponding DSN 2015 work; reviewed 2026-09-10
sources.locator: Abstract: relationships among pass bias, accumulated cycling, and read disturb
sources.limit: Only qualitative relationships are supported by the reviewed abstract. Unreviewed quantitative results are not reused, and 2Y nm MLC samples are not treated as equivalent to modern 3D QLC.

sources.label: Kioxia: BiCS FLASH Principles and Commercial Generations
sources.date: Page includes technical descriptions through 2023; reviewed 2026-09-10
sources.locator: Commercial-generation section; stacked electrodes, memory holes, and charge-storage film in Figures 4–5
sources.limit: 48 layers / 2015, 96 layers / 2018, 112 layers / 2020, and 162 layers / 2022 are the manufacturer's listed commercial history. This page is not treated as the latest 2026 layer-count ranking or a complete specification for each generation.

sources.label: KIOXIA: Schottky Source Contact and Hole Supply
sources.locator: Figures 1 and 4; GIDL hole supply from an N+ silicon source and the Schottky-contact alternative
sources.limit: Supports carrier supply and a named study; this diagram uses the conventional GIDL branch without merging in a Schottky source.

sources.label: SanDisk: GIDL-Assisted 3D NAND Erase
sources.locator: Figure 8 and GIDL erase description; terminal/select-gate bias difference, hole supply, and charge neutralization
sources.limit: Uses its own BL/SL and select-gate biases; do not substitute the floating-terminal erase conditions of US7696559B2.

variants.title: US7696559B2: Vertical String/Electron Tunneling
variants.summary: A string topology with an unfolded local film section. Erase follows source-line raising and electron release, not an asserted GIDL hole mechanism.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

variants.title: GIDL Assist: Hole Supply/Trap Neutralization
variants.summary: A positive terminal above the select-gate potential generates electron–hole pairs. Only the upper supply is expanded; the other end depends on the example. Separate from the older floating-terminal erase.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Red plus signs are holes; red arrows show hole motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: KIOXIA: Schottky Source Contact and Hole Supply
sources.locator: Figures 1 and 4; GIDL hole supply from an N+ silicon source and the Schottky-contact alternative
sources.limit: Supports carrier supply and a named study; this diagram uses the conventional GIDL branch without merging in a Schottky source.

sources.label: SanDisk: GIDL-Assisted 3D NAND Erase
sources.locator: Figure 8 and GIDL erase description; terminal/select-gate bias difference, hole supply, and charge neutralization
sources.limit: Uses its own BL/SL and select-gate biases; do not substitute the floating-terminal erase conditions of US7696559B2.

variants.caveat: A principle drawing redrawn from public sources, not a process cross-section to scale. Arrows represent the stated carrier or field; numerical design requires device-specific specifications.

operations.title: Read: Pass Unselected Cells and Sense the Selected Threshold
operations.summary: When one cell is read, the other storage cells still experience pass bias, so the absence of a program command does not mean zero read disturb. String resistance, wordline/bitline loading, and threshold-voltage distributions jointly affect readout. In US7696559B2, the selected 0 V condition belongs only to that early example; one fixed potential cannot distinguish all multilevel states.

sources.label: Toshiba: Columnar-Semiconductor Vertical NAND Patent US7696559B2
sources.locator: Figures 2 and 5–9; programming, erase, and bitline-discharge descriptions; claim 1
sources.limit: A specific early columnar-sidewall embodiment. It is not a substitute for every modern gate-all-around cross-section and is not a complete patent history of planar NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Flash Memory Fundamentals
sources.locator: Figures 2–5; floating-gate and charge-trap storage; threshold voltage and series-string reading
sources.limit: An introductory teaching source, not a complete operating specification for a particular chip. Generic illustrations do not establish the materials and biases of all planar or 3D NAND.

sources.label: Kioxia: Increasing Flash Capacity with Multilevel Cells
sources.locator: Figure 5 and adjacent text; bits per cell, threshold-voltage states, and speed/lifetime tradeoffs
sources.limit: Supports the requirement for 2 to the Nth power distinguishable states to store N bits and the qualitative tradeoffs. It does not provide universal endurance or speed ratios between TLC/QLC generations.

sources.label: Kioxia: Data Retention in the Managed Flash Endurance and Reliability Series
sources.locator: Pages 1–2; P/E cycling, temperature, and data retention
sources.limit: Supports evaluating NAND reliability under combined conditions. NAND values must not be transferred directly to EEPROM, SONOS, or OTP specifications.

sources.label: Kioxia: NAND Error-Correction Code Technical Brief
sources.locator: Page 1; raw NAND, managed NAND, and the role of ECC
sources.limit: Supports including error management in system comparisons. It does not supply a universal ECC strength, decoding latency, or spare-capacity ratio that can be applied directly throughout this material.

sources.label: Kioxia: Improving Memory-Hole Process Productivity with a New Etch Gas
sources.locator: Sections on memory-hole profile, etch rate, and high-aspect-ratio processing
sources.limit: Describes a specific deep-hole etching study and process bottlenecks. Its improvement figures are not extrapolated to all equipment, stack heights, or production costs.

sources.label: Y. Luo et al.: Early Retention Loss and Process Variation in 3D NAND
sources.locator: Abstract: layer-to-layer process variation, early retention loss, and retention interference
sources.limit: Only the abstract was reviewed to identify research questions. Unreviewed methods, sample counts, and quantitative improvements are not reused, and the distributions are not assumed to apply to all modern 3D NAND.

sources.label: Y. Cai et al.: Read-Disturb Errors in MLC NAND Flash
sources.date: Research account published 2018-05-08; corresponding DSN 2015 work; reviewed 2026-09-10
sources.locator: Abstract: relationships among pass bias, accumulated cycling, and read disturb
sources.limit: Only qualitative relationships are supported by the reviewed abstract. Unreviewed quantitative results are not reused, and 2Y nm MLC samples are not treated as equivalent to modern 3D QLC.

sources.label: Kioxia: BiCS FLASH Principles and Commercial Generations
sources.date: Page includes technical descriptions through 2023; reviewed 2026-09-10
sources.locator: Commercial-generation section; stacked electrodes, memory holes, and charge-storage film in Figures 4–5
sources.limit: 48 layers / 2015, 96 layers / 2018, 112 layers / 2020, and 162 layers / 2022 are the manufacturer's listed commercial history. This page is not treated as the latest 2026 layer-count ranking or a complete specification for each generation.

variants.title: US7696559B2: Vertical String/Electron Tunneling
variants.summary: A string topology with an unfolded local film section. Erase follows source-line raising and electron release, not an asserted GIDL hole mechanism.

legend.meaning: Blue minus signs are electrons; blue arrows show electron motion.
Orange E is electric field; green I is conventional current, opposite to electron motion.
Symbolic program, erase, and read biases; these are not numerical operating specifications.
FLT means floating; 0 is the reference potential chosen for the diagram.
CTL is the insulating charge-trap layer; Vₜ is read threshold. Yellow layers are dielectrics.

sources.label: Motorola: Toggle Writing Patent US6545906B1
sources.locator: Figures 4–6; SAF free layer, t0–t4 pulse sequence, and read-before-toggle description
sources.limit: Applies to the nearly balanced SAF toggle embodiment; drawn intermediate angles are illustrative.

variants.caveat: M1 is the free sublayer next to the barrier; its angle to REF determines P/AP. Intermediate angles and pulse heights are not measured. Rewriting the opposite data uses another toggle sequence, with no block erase.

legend.meaning: Conventional current, opposite to electron flow
Electron-flow direction, not a magnetization arrow
Free-layer / pinned-reference magnetization
Parallel low R / antiparallel high R; no logic encoding assigned

sources.label: IBM: Spin-Torque Structure Patent US5695864A
sources.locator: Abstract and claim 1: fixed and variable moments and current through the stack
sources.limit: An early magnetic structure, not a complete disclosure of modern perpendicular MgO MTJ processing.

sources.label: Katine et al.: Current-Driven Reversal in Co/Cu/Co Pillars
sources.locator: Abstract: electron flow from thin to thick layer favors AP; reverse flow favors P
sources.limit: Used for the current/electron-flow convention; not product data for an MgO MTJ.

variants.caveat: Here positive conventional current is upward and electron flow is free-to-reference, illustrating P→AP; reverse flow illustrates AP→P. Verify polarity for the actual stack. Switching probability and read disturbance are not quantified.

operations.title: SOT-MRAM · Write / SET

sources.label: imec: Functional SOT-MRAM Arrays and Cache Research

sources.limit: A research mechanism, not SOT volume production; the diagram explicitly includes an assist field and makes no field-free claim.

Explicit symmetry-breaking assist field in this example

sources.label: imec: Functional SOT-MRAM Arrays and Cache Research
sources.locator: Three-terminal SOT structure, separate read/write paths, and magnetic-field requirements
sources.limit: A research mechanism, not SOT volume production; the diagram explicitly includes an assist field and makes no field-free claim.

variants.caveat: Hassist is explicit; no deterministic field-free switching is assumed for a lone ideal line. I+/I− are opposite calibrated write directions; their state mapping depends on spin-Hall sign, stack orientation, and assist field.

variants.caveat: Tx denotes a qualitative crystallization region and Tm the melting point; curves and geometry are not measurements. Crystallization depends on temperature, time, and material; ordinary reads require neither melting nor restore.

legend.meaning: Word line / bit line / capacitor plate line
Two remanent polarization directions; no universal 0/1 mapping
Non-switching background charge / additional switching charge
Sense/restore amplifier, compared with an external reference

sources.label: Ramtron: Self-Restoring Ferroelectric Memory Patent US4873664A
sources.locator: Figure 3: 1T1C and reference branch; Figures 1/3 and read, latch, plate-line fall, and restore description
sources.limit: The two drawn branches are alternative initial states of one cell, not a merged circuit from Figures 3 and 4.

variants.caveat: This reverse operation directly rewrites polarization, without block erase. P↑/P↓ have no fixed 0/1 mapping; choose actual pulses for the ferroelectric material, stack, and effective switching condition.

operations.title: Capacitor FeRAM · Read and Restore
operations.summary: Distinguish switching and non-switching charge, latch the read value, then restore polarization as PL falls while WL stays enabled.

frames.title: Sense and Latch: Preserve the Original Data Decision
frames.caption: The sense amplifier compares against an external reference and latches. In this convention A drives BL to zero and B to V; both presently have P↑.
frames.state: Original data latched; B requires restore
